items.title: test(id): repair info_details malformed-hash regression test via factored reply parser
items.body: ## What The production half of #6633 (strict `active_module_hash` parsing in `WorldClient::info_details`) already landed on main via repo-keeper snapshot `4ecb3510c9` — but the regression test it arrived with calls a nonexistent `client.inject_json(...)` helper and uses an unimported `json!` macro, so the `id` lib-test target does not compile at all (14 errors; tracked as #6640 and #6643, duplicates of each other). This PR makes the coverage real: - Factors the `module_info` reply parsing out of `info_details` into `WorldClient::parse_module_info_reply` — **no production behavior change**: same fields, same error strings, same strictness. - Rewrites `info_details_rejects_malformed_active_module_hash` as a direct parser test covering every shape in the acceptance criteria: string → `Some(hash)`, `null` → `None`, missing field → `None`, and number / bool / array / object → `Err` naming the malformed `active_module_hash`. (Oracle: the parser's strictness for the sibling fields of the same reply.) ## Closes - Closes #6633 — its acceptance criteria are now all met on main + this PR (the fix itself landed in `4ecb3510c9`; this PR supplies the working regression tests). - Closes #6640 - Closes #6643 ## Verification - Laptop (worktree at this branch): `cargo test -p id --lib info_details_rejects_malformed_active_module_hash` — passes. - Laptop: `cargo test -p id --lib --no-run` — the lib-test target compiles again (it did not on main). Filed by the repo queue worker, lane code-a, in fallback mode (queue backend down 2026-11-06/07; issue #6633 was claimed via a fallback claim marker on the issue). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): reject world_created replies with a missing or mistyped created flag (#6632)
items.body: Fixes #6632. `WorldClient::create_world` read the `world_created` reply's outcome flag with a silent default — `reply["created"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false)` — so a reply whose `created` field was missing or mistyped (host bug, version skew) read as "the world already existed": `id world create` printed `exists` and exited 0 for a world whose creation was never confirmed. ## Change (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs`) - Factor the reply tail into `parse_create_world_reply`, following the `parse_module_info_reply` precedent (#6633): the refusal path still surfaces the host's message (or the existing default), a well-formed reply returns `Ok(true)`/`Ok(false)` unchanged, a missing `created` errors with "host sent no created flag in world_created reply", and a present-but-non-boolean `created` errors as a malformed `world_created` reply. Fail-closed is preserved — an unreadable flag never grants or confirms anything; the fix is visibility, not leniency. - Regression test `create_world_reply_requires_created_flag` drives the factored parser: both controls, missing flag, mistyped shapes (string / number / null / array), and both refusal shapes. Oracle: the sibling strictness of `parse_module_info_reply` — a present-but-wrong-shape field is corruption, not a default. ## Verification - Laptop (worktree @ 62377a73ee): `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml --lib create_world_reply` — `world_net::tests::create_world_reply_requires_created_flag` ok (1 passed). - Laptop: sibling parser test `info_details_rejects_malformed_active_module_hash` ok, and the existing create-world-over-iroh test `world_session::tests::tests::only_an_admin_creates_or_lists_worlds` ok (EXIT:0). - rustfmt clean on `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs`. Filed from a fallback-mode queue shift (queue backend down, code#6619): the issue was claimed and released via `fleet-claim` markers on #6632 by `repo-worker-code-l`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): refuse a mistyped module_hash in the admin history begin frame (#6641)
items.body: ## What `WorldClient::admin_event_history` read the `event_history_begin` frame's `module_hash` with `.as_str().map(...)` — every non-string value (number, bool, array, object) collapsed to `None`, the legitimate "world has no module" value, so a malformed export header silently recorded a world with a module as module-less (and `world_fixture::record` then baked that false provenance into the fixture header). Every sibling field in the same frame is strict; only this one was lenient. Issue #6642 is a duplicate of #6641 (same function, field, and evidence) and has been closed as a duplicate; this PR is the single fix for both. ## Change - Factor the begin-frame head parsing into `WorldClient::parse_event_history_begin` and give `module_hash` the same match-and-bail treatment `info_details` got for #6633: absent / `null` → `None`, string → `Some(hash)`, anything else → `Err` ("history reply has a malformed module_hash: expected string or null, got …"). No behavior change for conforming hosts (`ServerFrame::EventHistoryBegin` serializes the hash as string-or-null by construction). - Regression test `admin_event_history_begin_requires_a_string_or_null_module_hash`: string / null / missing controls plus number / bool / array / object refusals, with sibling fields verified intact. ## Verification (laptop, this branch) - `cargo test -p id --lib admin_event_history -- --test-threads=1`: new test passes. - `cargo test -p id --lib world_fixture -- --test-threads=1`: 28 passed, 0 failed (the fixture record/replay consumers). Closes #6641. Filed by the repo queue worker, lane code-a, in fallback mode (queue backend down 2026-11-06/07; issue #6641 claimed via a fallback claim marker on the issue). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved validation of event history headers, including checks for world IDs, sequence numbers, completeness, and event counts. * Event history headers now accept a missing or null module hash, while rejecting module hashes in unsupported formats.
